name: PEI-Canada Co-operation Agreement on Environmental and Impact Assessment
description: Canada and Prince Edward Island signed a co-operation agreement implementing a 'one project, one review' approach to streamline federal-provincial environmental and impact assessments for major projects, reducing regulatory duplication. PEI is the fourth province to sign such an agreement after BC, Ontario, and New Brunswick.

evidence.name: Prince Edward Island and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate major project assessments - Canada.ca

name: Charlottetown Official Plan Provincial Approval — 10-Storey Building Heights
description: PEI Land and Environment Minister Darlene Compton approved Charlottetown's new official plan, which allows buildings up to 10 storeys along high-traffic streets and intersections. The plan replaces the 1999 version and aims to increase housing density. City council must now develop a new zoning and development bylaw.

evidence.name: Developers may soon be able to build higher under Charlottetown's new official plan | CBC News

sources.title: Developers may soon be able to build higher under Charlottetown's new official plan | CBC News

name: PEI Electric School Bus Fleet Pause — Diesel Replacement Purchase
description: PEI paused electric school bus purchases and will instead buy 137 new diesel buses to replace aging fleet vehicles. PEI leads Canada with 33% fleet electrification (107 LION Electric buses) but cited charging infrastructure gaps (level-2 vs required level-3) and LION Electric's creditor protection as factors. The province maintains a 2030 full-electrification target.

evidence.name: Province pauses plans to buy new electric school buses for P.E.I.'s fleet in 2026 | CBC News

name: Charlottetown Hillsborough Street Transitional Housing Conversion
description: The PEI provincial government proposed renovating a six-unit building it owns on Hillsborough Street in Charlottetown into an 11-bed transitional housing facility. Charlottetown city council is considering the proposal.

name: PEI 2026-27 Capital Budget — Healthcare and Education Infrastructure
description: PEI's 2026-27 capital budget allocates $486.5 million for the fiscal year and $1.6 billion over five years, including $538 million for healthcare infrastructure, $65.4 million for three new elementary schools (East Royalty, West Royalty, Georgetown), $14.5 million for Parkside Elementary replacement design, and $92 million for French-language education facilities including $64 million to replace École Évangéline.
